title: Exact Values of the Six Trigonometric Functions at Standard Angles (Table I)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Without using a calculator, evaluate \sin\theta, \cos\theta, \tan\theta, \cot\theta, \sec\theta, and \csc\theta at each of the angles \theta = -\pi, -2\pi/3, 0, \pi/2, and 3\pi/4. State 'UND' wherever a function is undefined.

steps.title: Evaluate Sine and Cosine Using the Unit Circle
steps.explanation: Locate the terminal point (x, y) = (cos theta, sin theta) on the unit circle for each given angle using reference angles pi/3 and pi/4 and quadrant signs.
steps.why: On the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1, cos theta is the x-coordinate and sin theta is the y-coordinate.

steps.title: Compute Tangent and Cotangent Ratios
steps.explanation: Divide sin theta by cos theta to get tan theta (which is undefined at theta = pi/2 where cos theta = 0) and divide cos theta by sin theta to get cot theta (which is undefined at theta = -pi and 0 where sin theta = 0).
steps.why: Quotient identities define tan theta = sin theta / cos theta and cot theta = cos theta / sin theta whenever the denominator is nonzero.

steps.title: Compute Secant and Cosecant Reciprocals
steps.explanation: Take the reciprocals of cos theta and sin theta for each angle, marking 'UND' whenever the denominator equals zero.
steps.why: Reciprocal identities define sec theta = 1/cos theta and csc theta = 1/sin theta.
